name: Spring animation
definition: Motion driven by a simulated spring (mass, stiffness, damping) instead of a fixed duration, so the element settles rather than stopping on a schedule.
useWhen: motion should react to how it was interrupted, not a timer

sources.title: Spring Animations in Pure CSS with linear()
Chrome for Developers: the linear() easing function

notes: Head-adjacent but the searched word is usually 'spring animation'. Stiffness, damping ratio and mass are sub-vocabulary; damping is recorded separately, stiffness folded in here.

name: Overshoot
definition: The part of a motion that carries past its final value before coming back, the visual signature of an underdamped spring or a back easing curve.
useWhen: motion should read as having weight and momentum

implementations.name: cubic-bezier() with a control point outside 0 to 1

notes: Frequently confused with bounce; overshoot passes the target once, bounce oscillates around it.

name: Damping
definition: The friction term in a spring that decides how quickly oscillation dies out, from a loose wobble to a critically damped move with no bounce at all.
useWhen: tuning how much wobble a spring is allowed

sources.title: Spring Animations in Pure CSS with linear()

notes: Merge candidate with spring-animation if the taxonomy prefers one entry for the whole spring model.

name: Anticipation
definition: A small move in the opposite direction just before the main one, borrowed from character animation to telegraph what is about to happen.
useWhen: an action needs a wind-up so it does not start cold

sources.title: IxDF: UI Animation, applying Disney's 12 principles to UI

notes: One of the twelve Disney principles that survives translation to UI. GSAP's ScrollTrigger anticipatePin is an unrelated use of the same word.

name: Squash and stretch
definition: Deforming an element along its direction of travel so it reads as having mass and flexibility, usually as a press squash or a launch stretch.
useWhen: a control should feel physical when pressed or launched

sources.title: IxDF: UI Animation, applying Disney's 12 principles to UI

name: Follow-through
definition: Parts of a composition that keep moving briefly after the main element stops, and start slightly after it starts, so a group does not move as one rigid block.
useWhen: a group should move like connected parts, not one slab

sources.title: IxDF: UI Animation, applying Disney's 12 principles to UI

notes: Close to stagger (already on the site) but distinct: stagger offsets identical animations, follow-through is one motion dragging its dependents.

name: Arc motion
definition: Moving an element along a curved path rather than a straight line, so a change of position reads as natural rather than mechanical.
useWhen: an element travels in two axes at once

sources.title: IxDF: UI Animation, applying Disney's 12 principles to UI

name: FLIP
definition: A technique that measures an element's first and last positions, inverts the difference with a transform, then plays it off, so layout changes animate on the compositor.
useWhen: a layout change must animate without animating layout properties

sources.title: Josh Comeau: the FLIP technique for list animations

notes: Merge candidate with layout-animation: FLIP is the mechanism, layout animation is the feature name libraries ship it under.

name: Layout animation
definition: Animating an element between two layouts it was never explicitly positioned in, so reordering, resizing, or reflowing a list moves rather than jumps.
useWhen: the layout itself changed and the jump needs smoothing

sources.title: CSS-Tricks: animating layouts with the FLIP technique

notes: See flip-animation. Keep both only if the canonicalize step wants the technique and the feature separated.
resolved: absorbed by flip-animation as an alias

name: Shared element transition
definition: A transition where one element persists across two views and animates from its old position and size to its new one, tying the views together.
useWhen: the same thing appears in both the old and the new view
notes: 'hero animation' is a strong alias for the existing view-transition entry too.
resolved: folded into view-transition, which carries "shared element transition" and "hero animation"

name: Container transform
definition: Material's transition in which a container grows or shrinks into another one, its contents crossfading inside, so a card visibly becomes the screen it opened.
useWhen: a small surface opens into the larger one it belongs to

sources.title: Building beautiful transitions with Material Motion for Android

notes: One of Material's four named transition patterns (container transform, shared axis, fade through, fade).

name: Shared axis
definition: Material's transition where outgoing and incoming views slide and fade along the same x, y, or z axis, so direction encodes the navigational relationship.
useWhen: two views sit next to each other in a sequence or hierarchy

name: Fade through
definition: Material's transition for unrelated views: the outgoing view fades out completely before the incoming one fades in while scaling up slightly.
useWhen: two views have no spatial or hierarchical relationship
notes: Contrasts precisely with crossfade, where the two views overlap in opacity; the discrimination is the point of the entry.

name: Crossfade
definition: A transition in which one element fades out while the other fades in over the same span, so both are partly visible at the midpoint.
useWhen: swapping content of the same shape in place

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Merge candidate with dissolve; kept apart because dissolve is the single-element case and crossfade is the two-element case.

name: Dissolve
definition: A fade that carries the eye from one image or state to another without any movement, inherited from film editing vocabulary.
useWhen: the change should register without implying direction

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Merge candidate with crossfade.

name: Fade
definition: A change in opacity used to bring an element in or take it out, the cheapest transition and the one that implies no spatial relationship.
useWhen: an element appears or leaves without moving

name: Wipe
definition: A transition where a moving edge or mask travels across the frame, replacing what was there with what comes next.
useWhen: a reveal should have a visible leading edge

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

name: Morph transition
definition: A transition where a shape or icon is interpolated into a different shape rather than swapped, so the two states read as one object changing.
useWhen: two states are the same object in different forms

name: Icon morph
definition: An icon that animates between two meanings rather than cutting, such as a hamburger whose bars rotate into a close cross.
useWhen: one control carries two states and should show the change

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Strong long-tail search intent ('hamburger to X animation'); relates to the existing hamburger-menu entry.

name: Reveal animation
definition: Motion that uncovers content already in place, usually by growing a clip or mask outward from a point rather than moving the content itself.
useWhen: content should be uncovered rather than moved in

name: Entrance animation
definition: The motion an element plays as it arrives, running from a starting style that only exists before the element was ever rendered.
useWhen: something new appears and should not just pop in
notes: Could be merged with exit-animation into one 'enter and exit' entry, but the two have different hard problems and different APIs.

name: Exit animation
definition: The motion an element plays on its way out, which requires deferring its removal from the layout until the animation has finished.
useWhen: something is being removed and should not blink out

name: Slide transition
definition: A transition where content translates in or out along one axis, using direction to say whether the user moved forward, back, up, or down.
useWhen: the change has a direction the reader should feel

name: Push transition
definition: A navigation transition where the new view slides in and pushes the old one off, and reversing it pops back, encoding depth in a stack.
useWhen: navigating deeper into a stack and back out

name: Zoom transition
definition: A presentation that scales a tapped element up into the full view it opens, so the destination appears to come from the thing that was touched.
useWhen: the destination should visibly come from what was tapped
notes: Merge candidate with container-transform and shared-element-transition; kept because the platform word people search is 'zoom transition'.

name: Page transition
definition: Motion that covers a navigation between two whole pages or routes, replacing the hard cut a document load would otherwise produce.
useWhen: navigation between routes should feel continuous
notes: iframe because the subject is document scope: a real navigation inside the specimen document.

name: Cross-document view transition
definition: A view transition that spans an actual navigation between two documents, opted into by both pages so snapshots can be matched across the load.
useWhen: a multi-page site wants app-like navigation motion
notes: Cross-category with the existing view-transition entry; may be better as a section of that page than its own term. Sub-vocabulary worth capturing as aliases there: snapshot, image pair, ::view-transition-group, view-transition-class, transition types.
resolved: folded into view-transition (2026-08-15), which carries "MPA view transition"

name: Motion choreography
definition: The plan for how several animating elements relate in time and space, deciding what leads, what follows, and what stays still.
useWhen: more than one thing moves and the order matters
notes: The site's own attract mode uses 'choreography' as a code term; the dictionary sense here is the design-system one.

name: Motion token
definition: A named duration or easing value published by a design system, so timings are chosen from a set rather than typed per component.
useWhen: timings should be system decisions, not per-component ones

sources.title: Material Design 3: easing and duration tokens

notes: Overlaps the existing duration and easing entries; keep as the entry about naming and reuse, not about the values.

name: Cubic bezier
definition: The four-control-point curve that describes how a value moves between its start and end, the default way CSS spells an easing.
useWhen: an easing has to be written down exactly
notes: Sub-entry to the existing easing term; the standard curve family names (sine, quad, cubic, quart, quint, expo, circ, back, elastic, bounce, each in, out, in-out) belong as aliases on easing.

name: linear() easing
definition: An easing written as a list of sampled stops rather than a curve, which lets CSS express springs and bounces that no cubic bezier can describe.
useWhen: a curve is not expressible as one bezier

sources.title: Chrome for Developers: create complex animation curves with linear()
Smashing Magazine: the path to awesome CSS easing with linear()

name: Keyframe
definition: A point in an animation where a value is pinned, with the frames between generated by interpolating from one pinned point to the next.
useWhen: an animation needs waypoints, not just a start and end

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

name: Tween
definition: A single animation from one value to another over a duration, named for the in-between frames a computer fills in.
useWhen: naming one animation as a unit you can play or reverse

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Contrasts with spring: a tween is bounded by a duration, a spring by its physics.

name: Interpolation
definition: The rule that produces the intermediate values between two endpoints, which is why some properties can animate smoothly and others can only switch.
useWhen: explaining why a property will or will not animate
notes: The discrete case is exactly what transition-behavior: allow-discrete exists to work around.

name: Yo-yo loop
definition: A repeating animation that plays forward then backward instead of jumping back to the start, so a loop has no visible seam.
useWhen: a loop must repeat without a snap back to frame one

name: Bounce
definition: Motion that arrives, rebounds, and arrives again in decreasing amounts, reading as an object landing on a surface.
useWhen: an arrival should read as landing, with weight

name: Parallax
definition: Moving layers at different rates against the same input, so the slower layers read as farther away and the scene gains depth.
useWhen: depth should come from relative speed, not shadow
notes: One of the motions most often disabled under Reduce Motion, which makes it a good pair with the reduced-motion entry.

name: Scroll-linked animation
definition: An animation whose progress is bound to scroll position rather than to time, so scrolling back rewinds it exactly.
useWhen: the reader's scroll should drive the animation frame by frame
notes: The precise contrast with scroll-triggered-animation is the reason both entries exist.

name: Scroll-triggered animation
definition: An animation that scroll position only starts, after which it runs on its own clock and does not rewind when the reader scrolls back up.
useWhen: scrolling should start the motion, not steer it

sources.title: Chrome for Developers: CSS scroll-triggered animations are coming

notes: Usually built on IntersectionObserver, which is worth an alias but probably belongs to a different category's sweep.

name: View progress timeline
definition: A scroll timeline measured by one element's passage through the scrollport, with named ranges for entering, being contained, covering, and exiting.
useWhen: the animation should track one element, not the whole page
notes: Also carries the word 'scrollport', which may deserve its own layout-category entry.

name: Scrub
definition: Dragging an animation's playhead directly with an input such as the scrollbar, optionally with a lag so the animation catches up smoothly.
useWhen: an input should act as a transport control for motion
notes: Merge candidate with scroll-linked-animation; kept because 'scrub' is the word practitioners actually use.
resolved: folded (2026-08-15) into scroll-linked-animation, which carries the alias, while scrubbing owns the gesture word

name: Scroll pinning
definition: Holding a section fixed in place while the page keeps scrolling, spending scroll distance on an animation instead of on movement.
useWhen: a section should hold still while its content advances
notes: Cross-category with layout (position: sticky); recorded here because the searched concept is the scroll-motion technique.

name: Scrollytelling
definition: A narrative format where scrolling advances a story, with text steps driving a graphic that stays in view and changes as the reader descends.
useWhen: a story should advance at the reader's own scroll pace
notes: The scrollama URL is from memory and needs a probe. iframe because the demo wants the document scroller to be the reader's scroller.

name: Reduced motion
definition: A user preference asking software to cut non-essential animation, honored by swapping large movement for fades or by removing the motion entirely.
useWhen: motion could make someone dizzy or sick
notes: Cross-category with accessibility; recorded in motion because the demo is a motion demo. WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions is the related success criterion.
resolved: folded into prefers-reduced-motion, which carries "reduced motion"

name: Jank
definition: Visible stutter in motion caused by frames arriving late or not at all, so an animation that should be continuous reads as juddering.
useWhen: naming why smooth-looking motion feels wrong

sources.title: MDN: animation performance and frame rate
web.dev: jank busting for better rendering performance

name: Compositor-only animation
definition: An animation limited to properties the compositor can handle alone, usually transform and opacity, so it keeps running even when the main thread is busy.
useWhen: motion must stay smooth under load

sources.title: MDN: animation performance and frame rate

name: Motion path
definition: A defined path an element travels along, with its distance and rotation along that path animated instead of its x and y positions.
useWhen: an element should follow a specific route
notes: MDN notes the property was called motion-path in early drafts, which is exactly the naming confusion an entry can settle.

name: Ripple
definition: Touch feedback that expands a translucent circle outward from the exact point of contact, confirming where the press landed.
useWhen: a press needs confirmation at the point of contact
notes: Material 3 folds ripple into the broader 'state layer' concept, which is arguably a color-category term.

name: Pulse
definition: A slow repeating change in scale or opacity that keeps an element alive without moving it, used for waiting states and gentle attention.
useWhen: an element must signal life while nothing else happens

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Close to the existing shimmer entry; the discrimination is that shimmer sweeps and pulse does not move.

name: Shake
definition: A short lateral wobble used to reject an input, borrowed from the head shake and read as no rather than as an error message.
useWhen: an input is refused and should be felt, not just read

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

name: Jiggle mode
definition: An editing state announced by making every rearrangeable item wobble in place, so the whole screen says it can be reordered.
useWhen: an editing mode should be announced by motion alone

sources.title: How-To Geek: what is jiggle mode on iPhone

notes: Pure long tail: Apple has no official name, the community word is the entry. Good candidate for the 'what is the word for' framing.

name: Rubber banding
definition: Letting a scroll travel past its end with increasing resistance and then spring back, so the boundary is felt instead of hit.
useWhen: a scroll boundary should be felt, not just stopped at

sources.title: Smashing Magazine: scroll bouncing on your websites

notes: Android's equivalent is a stretch or edge glow rather than a bounce, which is a nice platform contrast for the article.
resolved: retired 2026-08-18: already an alias of overscroll, which carries "bounce scrolling"

name: Momentum scrolling
definition: Scrolling that keeps going after the finger lifts and decelerates to a stop, so a flick throws the content rather than dragging it.
useWhen: a flick should carry the content past the gesture
notes: Cross-category with interaction; the motion is the substance, so it is recorded here.

name: Interruptible animation
definition: Motion that can be caught, reversed, or redirected mid-flight from its current value, instead of finishing before it will accept a new input.
useWhen: a reader may act again before the motion finishes
notes: The strongest practical argument for springs over fixed durations, so it pairs with spring-animation.

name: Interactive transition
definition: A transition whose progress is held by an ongoing gesture, so the reader can drag it partway, hesitate, and either complete it or send it back.
useWhen: a gesture should own the transition until it is released
notes: Cross-category with interaction; kept here because the term names how the transition is driven.

name: Directionality
definition: The rule that every movement carries a direction, and that using it consistently tells the reader how the parts of an interface relate.
useWhen: motion should say where a view sits relative to another

name: Marquee
definition: Text or logos that scroll continuously across a strip, either as a decorative ticker or because a label is too long for its box.
useWhen: content is wider than its box and must still be read

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: The deprecated <marquee> element is worth a disambiguation note in the article body.

name: Ken Burns effect
definition: A slow pan and zoom across a still image that gives it motion, named after the documentary filmmaker who made the technique famous.
useWhen: a static image needs life without becoming video

name: Typewriter effect
definition: Revealing text one character at a time, as if it were being typed, usually with a blinking caret trailing the last letter.
useWhen: text should arrive as if being written right now

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Has picked up a second life as the way streamed model output is rendered, which is a useful contemporary note.

name: Count-up animation
definition: Animating a number toward its value instead of setting it, often with digits rolling like an odometer so the change is legible.
useWhen: a number changing should be noticed and read

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Search intent is strong ('rolling number animation') and no system owns the name; verify implementations in a later pass.

name: Confetti burst
definition: A short particle celebration thrown across the screen to mark a completion, decorative by design and the first thing reduced motion should drop.
useWhen: a milestone deserves a moment of celebration

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

name: Collapsing toolbar
definition: A header that shrinks as the page scrolls, trading its large title and image for a compact bar that stays available.
useWhen: a header must stay reachable without keeping its height
notes: Cross-category candidate with component; relates directly to the existing app-bar entry.

name: Attract mode
definition: A self-playing loop an idle screen falls into to demonstrate itself, inherited from arcade cabinets and reused by kiosks and product demos.
useWhen: an unattended screen should demonstrate itself

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: The site's own stage uses this word, which makes the entry self-demonstrating. Could sit in pattern instead of motion.

name: Microinteraction
definition: A single small loop of trigger, rule, feedback, and mode built around one task, where the feedback is usually the motion people remember.
useWhen: naming the smallest complete unit of interaction design
notes: Cross-category: belongs to interaction, surfaced here because every motion source defines it. Expect a duplicate from the interaction sweep.

name: Layout shift
definition: Content moving after it was already visible because something above it loaded or grew, which is motion nobody asked for.
useWhen: content jumps under the reader after it appeared

sources.title: web.dev: jank busting for better rendering performance

notes: Cross-category: recorded as layout, discovered in the motion sweep. It is the negative case that the site's own no-incidental-layout-shift rule is about.

name: Scroll snap
definition: Scrolling that comes to rest on defined positions rather than anywhere, so a flick always lands on a whole item.
useWhen: a scroll should always end on a whole item
notes: Cross-category: interaction or layout rather than motion, but it turned up through every scroll-motion source.

name: Lottie
definition: A JSON format for vector animations exported from design tools and played natively on the web and mobile, so complex motion ships without video.
useWhen: designed animation must ship as an asset, not as code

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: A format rather than a design concept; drop it if the taxonomy excludes tooling. demo: none because there is nothing to illustrate without shipping the runtime.

name: Hover lift
definition: A card or button that rises a few pixels and deepens its shadow while the pointer is over it, so the whole surface reads as lifted toward the reader.
useWhen: a whole surface should answer the pointer, not just its border

sources.title: Subframe: CSS card hover effect examples

notes: Round two: named in round one's residue list. Transform plus shadow only, never margin or top, so the row it sits in does not move (SPEC §5).

name: Magnetic button
definition: A control that leans toward the cursor as it approaches, translating a fraction of the distance to its centre so it reads as attracted rather than merely hovered.
useWhen: a hero control should feel alive before it is clicked

sources.title: Init HTML: magnetic hover effect, cursor-attracted buttons

notes: Distinct from hover lift: the displacement tracks pointer position, so it needs pointermove plus a spring back to rest when the pointer leaves.

name: Cursor follower
definition: A dot or ring that trails the pointer with a lag and often swells over links, replacing or augmenting the native cursor as a piece of brand motion.
useWhen: the pointer itself is part of the site's personality

sources.title: Webflow: a guide to custom cursors
HubSpot: how to use custom animated cursors

notes: An accessibility hazard as much as a vocabulary item: hiding the native cursor costs pointer visibility. The stage already draws its own ghost cursor, so a demo of this must not fight it.

name: Fill mode
definition: Whether an animation's first or last keyframe styles apply outside its running window, which decides if an element snaps back when it finishes or stays where it landed.
useWhen: an animation ends and the element must not jump back
notes: Round one flagged it as felt behaviour rather than syntax: the word names what a reader sees when an animation ends and the element snaps back to where it started.

name: Delay
definition: The wait between an animation being triggered and starting to move, the unit stagger is built from and the reason a hover effect reads as either twitchy or considered.
useWhen: motion should start after something else, not with it
notes: The missing sibling of the existing site terms duration and easing. Canonicalize may prefer to fold it into duration rather than ship a third timing atom.

name: Stepped animation
definition: Motion that jumps between a fixed number of discrete positions instead of interpolating, the mechanic behind sprite sheets, ticking clock hands and segmented spinners.
useWhen: the movement should tick rather than glide
notes: The counterexample that makes easing legible: an animation with no in-betweens at all.

name: Height animation
definition: Animating a container between collapsed and its content's natural size, long impossible because height auto did not interpolate and now opened up by interpolate-size and calc-size().
useWhen: a section must grow to fit content without a magic pixel value

sources.title: Chrome for Developers: animate to height: auto

notes: The motion half of the existing accordion site term; canonicalize should decide which of the two owns the collapse animation.

name: Origin-aware animation
definition: Scaling or fading a panel out of the control that opened it by putting its transform origin on that anchor, so the panel reads as belonging to its trigger.
useWhen: a menu should look like it came from its button
notes: The reason a popover placed by a positioning library still needs its origin set: placement alone does not tell the motion where it came from.

name: Pop in
definition: An entrance that scales slightly past full size before settling, so the element arrives with a small snap instead of simply being there.
useWhen: an arriving element should feel eager rather than merely present
notes: Overlaps entrance-animation and overshoot; kept because 'pop in' is what people ask for by name. Merge candidate.

name: Asymmetric easing
definition: Giving a state change and its reverse different curves or durations, usually a quick confident exit and a slower entrance, so the two directions do not feel identical.
useWhen: opening and closing should not be mirror images
notes: Sits between easing and motion-token: the token sets say the same thing with named accelerate and decelerate curves.

name: Perceptual duration
definition: How long a spring appears to take, measured to the point the movement stops being visible rather than to its mathematical rest, the figure to quote against a timed animation.
useWhen: a spring must be compared with a duration
notes: The word that makes a spring reviewable: without it a designer cannot answer 'how long is this'.

name: Frame rate
definition: How many frames a second the interface actually draws, the budget every animation spends: 60fps leaves about 16ms per frame and a 120Hz display halves it.
useWhen: motion has to be judged in milliseconds per frame

sources.title: MDN: animation performance and frame rate

notes: Jank already records the symptom; this records the unit. Merge candidate if the taxonomy wants one performance word.

name: Layout thrashing
definition: Reading a geometric value after writing to the DOM in the same frame, forcing the browser to lay out synchronously over and over and stalling the animation that caused it.
useWhen: an animation stutters and the cause is the code, not the curve

sources.title: web.dev: avoid large, complex layouts and layout thrashing
Paul Irish: what forces layout / reflow

notes: Distinct from layout-shift: nothing moves that should not, the frames simply never arrive on time.

name: Line drawing animation
definition: An SVG stroke that appears to draw itself by animating its dash offset along its own length, used for signatures, check marks and illustrated line art.
useWhen: a mark should look drawn rather than revealed

sources.title: CSS-Tricks: how SVG line animation works

notes: The dash trick is the whole term: stroke-dasharray as long as the path, then animate stroke-dashoffset to zero.

name: Motion blur
definition: Blurring an element along its direction of travel so fast movement reads as speed instead of teleporting, borrowed from film and rare but real in interfaces.
useWhen: something moves fast enough that a sharp frame looks wrong

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Expensive on the web: filter: blur() is not a compositor-only property, which is half of why the term is rarer here than in film.

name: Float animation
definition: A slow continuous up and down drift on an idle element so a static composition keeps breathing without asking for attention.
useWhen: a hero illustration should not look frozen
notes: Ambient motion: nothing triggers it and nothing ends it, which is exactly what reduced motion should switch off.

name: Orbit animation
definition: One element circling another on a continuous path, used for logo constellations and loading states where the revolving is the ornament.
useWhen: elements should revolve around a fixed centre
notes: Slug is orbit-animation because interaction.json already owns 'orbit' for the three-finger camera gesture.

name: 3D tilt
definition: Rotating a card in perspective toward the pointer so it appears to tip in three dimensions, often with a moving highlight to sell the depth.
useWhen: a card should read as a physical object under the pointer
notes: Slug avoids 'tilt' because interaction.json uses that word for the device gesture. Perspective and transform-origin are folded in here rather than recorded as separate atoms.

name: Modal presentation
definition: The slide-up-over transition that puts a sheet or dialog in front of the current screen while what is behind recedes, the platform motion for entering a modal context.
useWhen: a task takes over the screen and must be dismissible
notes: Captured from uiterms.com in round one. Push transition, parallax and spring easing from that same capture were already recorded, so this was the only new one.

name: Smooth scrolling
definition: Animating a programmatic jump so the page travels to its destination instead of cutting there, which keeps an anchor link or a back-to-top button from losing the reader's place.
useWhen: a jump would leave the reader unsure where they landed
notes: demo: iframe because the subject is a document scroller, which is exactly the case SPEC allows the expensive isolation mode for. Do not confuse with the smoothed custom scrolling that earns the name scroll hijacking (recorded in interaction.json).

name: Sliding indicator
definition: A single underline or pill that travels between tabs to mark the selection instead of each tab drawing its own, so the move itself says which way the selection went.
useWhen: selection should move between items rather than blink between them

sources.title: CSS-Tricks: creating an animated menu indicator with CSS selectors

notes: The motion half of the existing segmented-control and tabs site terms; the kit's <sp-segmented> already carries the state this would animate.

name: Dock magnification
definition: Scaling each item in a row by how close the pointer is to it, so the hovered item swells, its neighbours ramp down, and the row reads as bulging under the cursor.
useWhen: a dense row of icons needs a hovered target enlarged in place

sources.title: O'Reilly, jQuery 1.4 Animation: resizing elements and the fisheye menu

notes: New systemId buildui. A layout-shift trap by construction: the honest version reserves the row's full magnified height so the page below never moves (SPEC §5).

name: Split-flap animation
definition: A digit or letter changing by flipping through the characters between the old value and the new one, imitating the mechanical boards of airports and flip clocks.
useWhen: a changing value should read as mechanical rather than digital

sources.title: Design engineering: a split-flap display component

notes: Distinct from count-up: the value does not interpolate, it steps through every character in between, which is why it pairs with stepped-animation.

name: Gooey effect
definition: Blurring a group of shapes and then crushing the blur back to a hard edge so overlapping elements merge into one liquid silhouette as they move apart and together.
useWhen: two moving shapes should read as one substance

sources.title: Animation Patterns: SVG metaball gooey filter with feColorMatrix

notes: The alpha-contrast half of the filter is unsupported in Safari and Firefox, so the fallback is a plain blur. Good candidate for a specimen that shows the filter chain in two steps.

name: Spotlight hover
definition: A soft radial glow centred on the pointer's position inside a card, lighting its surface and border as the cursor moves and going dark when the cursor leaves.
useWhen: a card should light up under the pointer rather than change colour

sources.title: Frontend Masters: how to build a glowing hover effect that follows the pointer
Cruip: how to create a spotlight card hover effect with Tailwind CSS

notes: Mechanically a pair of CSS custom properties updated on pointermove, which is why it is motion rather than colour: nothing is restyled, a gradient is repositioned.

name: Stacking cards
definition: A run of sections that each stick at the top of the viewport as the next one slides over it, so scrolling deals the page like a deck rather than passing it by.
useWhen: sequential sections should pile up instead of scrolling away

sources.title: CSS-Tricks: stacked cards with sticky positioning

notes: demo: iframe because the subject is the document scroller and a run of sticky sections needs the page's own scroll, not a nested one.

name: Predictive back
definition: A back gesture that reveals the destination underneath while the finger is still down, so the swipe can be finished or abandoned once the reader has seen where it goes.
useWhen: a back swipe should show its destination before it commits
notes: The platform's own name for a gesture-driven interruptible transition, which is why it is worth recording next to interactive-transition rather than folded into it.

name: Additive animation
definition: Composing an animation on top of whatever is already animating the same property instead of replacing it, so a second nudge adds to the first rather than restarting it.
useWhen: a repeated trigger should stack rather than snap back to the start

sources.title: CSS-Tricks: additive animation with the Web Animations API

notes: Deep vocabulary, but it is the reason a rapidly retriggered nudge or shake reads as one motion instead of a stutter.

name: Velocity skew
definition: Skewing or stretching content in proportion to how fast the page is scrolling and easing it back to square when the scroll stops, so speed shows up in the shape of the content.
useWhen: scroll speed itself should be visible

sources.title: GSAP forums: skew on scroll velocity

notes: Squash and stretch applied to a scroller: the same animation principle, driven by input velocity rather than a curve.

name: Page curl
definition: A page turn that lifts and bends the leaf away from the spine as the finger drags it, the most literal transition a reader can be given.
useWhen: turning a page should read as paper rather than as a slide

sources.title: MacRumors: re-enable the classic page turning animation in Apple Books
Creating a page curl transition in SwiftUI

notes: Apple Books offers Curl, Slide and None, which is the clearest evidence the word names a choice rather than a decoration. Effectively absent from the web, so a specimen would be an approximation.

name: Card flip
definition: Rotating a card about its own axis to show a second face on the back, with the hidden face pre-rotated and its backface hidden so only one side is ever visible.
useWhen: one surface carries two faces and both are the same object

sources.title: David DeSandro: card flip, intro to CSS 3D transforms
Auroratide: a (more) realistic card flip animation

notes: Not to be confused with the existing flip-animation entry, which records the FLIP technique (First Last Invert Play). Two unrelated meanings of one word, and the collision is itself worth writing about.

name: Parenting
definition: Tying one element's motion to another's so moving or scaling the parent carries the child with it, which is how a group of parts reads as one object instead of several.
useWhen: several elements must move as one because one of them leads

sources.title: UX Magazine: creating usability with motion, the UX in Motion Manifesto
Issara Willenskomer: the UX in Motion Manifesto

notes: One of the twelve UX in Motion principles. accessibility.json already uses 'reparenting' for the unrelated DOM-order sense, which canonicalize should keep apart.

name: Cloning
definition: Spawning a new element visibly out of an existing one so the reader can see where it came from, rather than having it arrive from nowhere.
useWhen: a new object must be traceable to the thing that made it

sources.title: UX Magazine: creating usability with motion, the UX in Motion Manifesto
The 12 principles of UX in motion

notes: Close to origin-aware-animation and container-transform; the distinction is that the source stays put and a copy leaves it. Merge candidate.

name: Dimensionality
definition: Giving interface objects a believable place in depth by folding, layering or flipping them, so a reader can tell where something went and where it will come back from.
useWhen: objects need somewhere to come from and return to

sources.title: UX Magazine: creating usability with motion, the UX in Motion Manifesto
The 12 principles of UX in motion

notes: Easy to confuse with the existing directionality entry: that one is about which way, this one is about how many dimensions the interface pretends to have.

name: Dolly and zoom
definition: Borrowing the camera's vocabulary: dolly moves the viewer through the scene, zoom scales the scene itself, and the interface reads as travelling rather than rearranging.
useWhen: the reader should feel moved through the interface

sources.title: UX Magazine: creating usability with motion, the UX in Motion Manifesto
School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: The film loan that explains zoom-transition and ken-burns-effect; keep only if the taxonomy wants the camera metaphor named as such.
